cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose getSchemaLocation().toString() equals "http://example.com/schema.json"
cases.description: Happy‑path: a well‑formed URI and a simple JSON schema node should result in a non‑null JsonSchema with the correct location.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose getSchemaLocation().toString() equals "" (empty string)
cases.description: Edge case: an empty string URI is still accepted; the factory should create a JsonSchema with an empty location.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose getSchemaLocation().toString() contains "space in name" after decoding
cases.description: URI with encoded spaces – verify that the location is stored correctly after normalization.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose meta‑schema is Draft‑07 (as indicated by $schema) and location equals "urn:example:schema"
cases.description: Non‑hierarchical URI (URN) with a $schema keyword – ensures the factory forwards the node unchanged.
Passing a null URI should cause the method to throw NPE because SchemaLocation.of(null) cannot be created.
Passing a null JsonNode should result in NPE when newJsonSchema attempts to process the node.
Both parameters null – the first null encountered (schemaUri) should trigger the exception.

cases.expected: URISyntaxException wrapped in IllegalArgumentException (or RuntimeException) when SchemaLocation.of throws
cases.description: A syntactically invalid URI should cause the factory to fail early, propagating the exception.

group: Complex schema node with definitions and $ref

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose meta‑schema is Draft‑07, location equals "http://example.com/complex.json", and internal $ref resolution works (i.e., the schema contains a resolved definition for "age")
cases.description: A schema containing definitions and a $ref should be loaded correctly; the factory must preserve the $ref so that later validation can resolve it.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose getSchemaLocation().toString() equals "https://example.org/schema.json?version=1#section2"
cases.description: Verify that query strings and fragments are preserved in the stored SchemaLocation.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose getSchemaLocation().toString() equals "http://example.com/über.json" (the Unicode character is correctly retained after normalization)
cases.description: A URI containing non‑ASCII characters should survive the factory’s normalization unchanged.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema representing a boolean true schema (i.e., any instance validates successfully)
cases.description: JSON Schema draft‑07 allows a schema to be a literal boolean; the factory should accept a JsonNode that is the literal true.

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema representing a boolean false schema (i.e., no instance validates successfully)
cases.description: A literal false schema should be accepted and reflected in the created JsonSchema.
A schema node that is a JSON string (neither object nor boolean) is not a valid JSON Schema; the factory should reject it with an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Unknown $schema IRI – fallback to default meta‑schema

cases.expected: instance of JsonSchema whose meta‑schema defaults to the library's latest supported version (e.g., Draft‑07) because the provided $schema IRI cannot be resolved
cases.description: When the $schema keyword points to an IRI that the factory does not recognise, it should fall back to the default meta‑schema rather than throwing an exception.

group: Invalid inputs – unsupported json node types

cases.description: A JsonNode that is a numeric literal (neither object nor boolean) is not a valid JSON Schema; the factory should reject it with IllegalArgumentException.
A JsonNode that is a JSON array (neither object nor boolean) is invalid as a top‑level schema; the factory must throw IllegalArgumentException.
